text: Deadlines are a part of professional life, and handling them well comes down to a few key skills. First, good time management means breaking a large project into smaller tasks and scheduling them over several days, rather than trying to finish everything at the last minute. Next, prioritization is crucial; you need to identify which tasks are most important and tackle those first. Scope management is also vital—if a project grows beyond what was agreed, you should politely refuse or negotiate what can be delayed. Finally, clear communication with your team or client is essential. If you foresee a problem, speak up early. It is far better to update someone in advance than to surprise them later.
